prompt: A movie theater chain wants to set prices for a new premium recliner seat. The candidate's framework: (1) Strengths; (2) Weaknesses; (3) Opportunities; (4) Threats. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: It's a generic SWOT: no customer value, rival prices or seat cost
options.feedback: Right. Pricing needs customer value, competitor prices and cost.

options.text: Buckets 2 and 4 overlap: in this SWOT, weak sales are also a threat
options.feedback: Weaknesses are internal and threats are external. The issue is that a SWOT doesn't fit pricing.

options.text: Missing: a SWOT bucket for the cost of the recliners
options.feedback: Adding one bucket doesn't turn a SWOT into a pricing framework.

options.text: Bucket 4 doesn't belong: competitors' threats don't set a seat price
options.feedback: Competitor prices actually matter for pricing. The issue is that the whole SWOT is generic.

explanation: SWOT is a generic strategy list. A price needs value to customers, alternatives, cost, and the effect on regular seat sales.

extras.corrected_framework: Customer willingness to pay; competitor premium seats; cost of seats and space; cannibalization of regular seats
